run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: OpenTelemetry Demo Astronomy Shop
Namespace: astronomy-shop

An online shopping platform built with a microservices architecture, showcasing OpenTelemetry instrumentation for distributed tracing across services.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The astronomy-shop stack was freshly deployed at 11:07:32Z; every workload was at Deployment revision 1 except frontend-proxy, which was rolled a second time at 11:08:29Z-11:08:32Z (new ReplicaSet frontend-proxy-88764bfbb) with the same image tag ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.2.0-frontend-proxy but a different pod template: Envoy was replaced by a Perl 'edge request filter' whose env carries WAF_RULE_REGEX=^([a-zA-Z]+)*$ and WAF_RULE_ENABLED=true. Immediately after that swap the edge hop became the latency bottleneck: in Jaeger traces at 11:08:30.9-11:08:31.4Z (old Envoy pod serving) a load-generator user action took 11.0-14.6 ms with the frontend server span at 6.7-10.7 ms and HTTP 200; for requests issued 11:08:36.9-11:08:42.1Z (after the swap) the same load-generator client spans took 13.1-17.3 s while the matching frontend server spans lasted only 6.4-62.2 ms and still returned HTTP 200 - e.g. a load-generator POST starting at 11:08:37.71Z reached the frontend at 11:08:54.23Z, a ~16.5 s queue at the only hop between them, the frontend-proxy. No errors were observed inside the read window (locust failure counters 0 at 11:08:48Z, all 27 pods Running/ready with 0 restarts), so the observed impact is a large latency regression at the edge, not failures. Competing explanations were checked and rejected: all flagd feature flags are in defaultVariant off, the Kafka 'orders' topic exists with two STABLE consumer groups (the 'Unknown topic or partition' line was a boot-time race), and the connection refusals in pod logs fall in the 11:07:45-11:08:11Z startup phase only. The precise internal mechanism (single-threaded serialization, and/or catastrophic backtracking in the nested-quantifier WAF regex) is a hypothesis because the replacement proxy emits no spans, and a query of its logs returned nothing.

claims.text: All 23 astronomy-shop Deployments were created at 2026-11-21T11:07:32Z, and only frontend-proxy is at generation 2 with annotation deployment.kubernetes.io/revision=2; every other Deployment reports generation 1 / revision 1.

Deployment frontend-proxy has two ReplicaSets: frontend-proxy-579d54f6f5 (created 11:07:35Z) running Envoy via command "/bin/sh -c envsubst < envoy.tmpl.yaml | sed ... > envoy.yaml && exec envoy -c envoy.yaml", and frontend-proxy-88764bfbb (created 11:08:29Z) running command ["/usr/bin/perl","-e"] with a Perl 'edge request filter' script and env WAF_RULE_REGEX=^([a-zA-Z]+)*$ and WAF_RULE_ENABLED=true; both use image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.2.0-frontend-proxy.

The current frontend-proxy Deployment pod template carries env WAF_RULE_REGEX="^([a-zA-Z]+)*$" and WAF_RULE_ENABLED="true" and command ["/usr/bin/perl","-e"], reports observedGeneration 2 and 1 ready/updated replica, with Progressing condition message "ReplicaSet frontend-proxy-88764bfbb has successfully progressed" at 11:08:32Z.

Deployment events for frontend-proxy show "Scaled up replica set frontend-proxy-88764bfbb from 0 to 1" at 11:08:29Z and "Scaled down replica set frontend-proxy-579d54f6f5 from 1 to 0" at 11:08:32Z; in the same event set no other astronomy-shop Deployment has a second scale-up, so only frontend-proxy was rolled after the initial 11:07:32-11:07:35Z deployment.

Events record pod frontend-proxy-579d54f6f5-6src6 reason Killing at 11:08:32Z and ReplicaSet frontend-proxy-579d54f6f5 reason SuccessfulDelete message "Deleted pod: frontend-proxy-579d54f6f5-6src6" at 11:08:32Z, i.e. the Envoy-based pod was replaced by its own controller during the rollout.

Baseline before the proxy swap: Jaeger traces between 11:08:30.938Z and 11:08:31.393Z show load-generator operation user_index with duration 14627 microseconds and its frontend GET span 10706 microseconds (http.status_code=200), and user_browse_product 11000 microseconds with frontend GET /api/products/{productId} 6740 microseconds (200); the frontend server spans' parent span (spanID a23338aa49b09ad3 / 499a0320b88c94e5) is not visible in the sampled view.

After the swap, for requests the load generator initiated between 11:08:36.894Z and 11:08:42.117Z, its own client spans lasted 13,138,023-17,325,677 microseconds (13.1-17.3 s) while the corresponding frontend server spans lasted only 6,351-62,155 microseconds and returned http.status_code=200; in trace 7c4d0a4ea036dfe41745f056c1c0b70c the load-generator POST span starts at 1795259317706884 and the frontend POST /api/product-ask-ai-assistant/[productId]/index span only starts at 1795259334231000, a gap of about 16.5 s on the hop between them.

In those post-swap traces the frontend server span's parent reference points directly at the load-generator client span (frontend span 2da6b453563dbd9a parent spanID 15e427ad7bda972b, service load-generator), so no intermediate edge span is emitted by the replacement proxy while the 16.5 s delay occurs.
All 27 astronomy-shop pods, including frontend-proxy-88764bfbb-7tqqs, are in phase Running with all containers ready=true and restartCount 0 at the observation time 11:08:51Z.

Startup-phase only: pod logs between 11:07:45Z and 11:08:11Z show connection refusals (frontend ECONNREFUSED to 10.96.198.20:8080 checkout, 10.96.116.77:8080 cart, 10.96.144.212:8080 ad, 10.96.171.254:8080 product-catalog; recommendation failing to reach product-catalog 10.96.171.254:8080; product-reviews tool call failing to postgresql 10.96.127.252:5432) and accounting logging 'Consume error: Subscribed topic not available: orders: Broker: Unknown topic or partition' at 11:08:11Z.

At the end of the read window the load generator reports no failed requests: locust_requests_fail_ratio is 0 at 11:08:48Z and all 37 locust_requests_num_failures series (including name="Aggregated") are 0 at 11:08:48Z.

Root-cause mechanism: the frontend-proxy pod template change replaced the Envoy edge proxy with a single-threaded Perl filter that handles one accepted connection at a time, so concurrent front-end traffic queues at the edge; this queuing accounts for the 13.1-17.3 s client-observed latency while the frontend served each request in milliseconds. The pod template also sets WAF_RULE_ENABLED=true, which in the container script makes every request carrying a waf= query parameter short-circuit to a synthetic "200 ok" instead of being proxied, and its rule ^([a-zA-Z]+)*$ is a nested-quantifier regex subject to catastrophic backtracking that could stall the single process; neither the short-circuit nor backtracking was directly observed in this run.

Feature-flag fault injection via flagd is not the cause: every flag in ConfigMap flagd-config (including adFailure, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, imageSlowLoad, failedReadinessProbe) has defaultVariant "off".

A missing Kafka 'orders' topic is not the cause of a sustained incident: the topic now exists (1 partition, not internal) and the accounting and fraud-detection consumer groups are in state STABLE, so the 11:08:11Z 'Unknown topic or partition' line was a startup race during the 11:07:32Z deployment.

A backend service outage is not supported as the cause of the post-swap latency: the sampled post-swap traces show cart (POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart), product-catalog (oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct), product-reviews and the frontend API routes answering with grpc status 0 / HTTP 200 in single-digit to tens of milliseconds, and the slow segment lies entirely before the frontend server span starts.

Within the read window the observed symptom was latency, not errors: no error spans appear among the sampled post-swap traces (all requests returned http.status_code=200 or rpc.grpc.status_code=0) and the load generator's failure counters were 0 at 11:08:48Z.

gaps: The authorized window ends at 2026-11-21T11:08:48Z, only ~19 s after the frontend-proxy rollout completed, so whether the edge latency escalates into timeouts, 5xx responses or a rising locust fail_ratio after that instant is unknown.

The replacement Perl proxy is not instrumented: post-swap frontend spans reference the load-generator span as their parent instead of an edge span, and the log query for pod frontend-proxy-88764bfbb-7tqqs returned nothing (status no_data, 0 lines), so the proxy's internal per-request time, its 'request_filter_eval' output and any WAF-rule evaluation were not observed.

What object or actor patched Deployment frontend-proxy to revision 2 could not be established: the change_history integration is not available in this Run, and the Kubernetes events only show the resulting ReplicaSet scale-up/scale-down.

Metric coverage is thin: queries for traces_span_metrics_calls_total over 24h, 50m and 10m ranges, http_server_request_duration_seconds_count, and kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready all returned no_data, and the span-metric series only exists as instant values at 11:08:48Z, so the latency baseline had to come from Jaeger traces and no app metric series spans the pre-rollout period.

The otel-collector-agent DaemonSet is also at generation 2 with pods replaced at 11:08:16-11:08:22Z (SuccessfulDelete/SuccessfulCreate events) and its collectors logged connection refusals to opensearch:9200 and otel-collector:4318; what triggered that change is not established and it showed no link to the front-end latency.
No payment service span was present in the sampled traces, so payment was not verified beyond its pod being Running/ready with 0 restarts.
next_steps: Compare Deployment frontend-proxy revision 1 and revision 2 (env, command, resources) to confirm the intended configuration change and revert the pod template to the Envoy-based proxy.

Reproduce the ReDoS with a request such as GET /?waf=<long alphabetic string><non-alphabetic char> against the frontend-proxy service and observe whether the single Perl process stalls, and test whether requests carrying waf= are answered with the synthetic "200 ok" instead of a proxied page.

If an edge filter is required, make it concurrent (multiple workers or an event loop), bound the regex evaluation (linear-time matcher or non-nested rule) and restore OTel tracing so the edge hop stays observable.
Continue monitoring locust_requests_fail_ratio and locust_requests_current_response_time_percentile_95 after 11:08:48Z to quantify end-user impact and confirm recovery after the template is reverted.
